mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by monthly PAYEMS exceeding 130,000 for three consecutive months predicts stronger consumer demand and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the employment signal (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 93.0 for two consecutive months indicates accelerating supply capacity, which amplifies investor optimism and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 93.0 and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 218 for two consecutive months, it signals a supply-side inflation pressure that the Fed is likely to counter with rate hikes, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 218 and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% indicate labor market tightening that often coincides with higher equity valuations and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-tightening periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in housing starts (not available in the provided proxies - skip this) — instead, use HOUST: When HOUST exceeds 600 for two consecutive months, it reflects robust demand for consumer durable goods, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 600 and remains above for 2 months

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand (GDPC1) above their respective 90th percentiles for two consecutive months create a synergistic effect that amplifies growth expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 99.4 and GDPC1 > 118.2 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary policy easing regime (FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months), the convergence of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 215) and strong industrial production (INDPRO > 95) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 months AND CPIAUCSL < 215 AND INDPRO > 95
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in the specified regime (t-test p > 0.05).
